scope: Production browser worker inference on a fixed EWT syntax regression fixture consulted during tokenizer development, plus newly authored development challenges and controlled gold-guided agreement mutations. The syntax fixture remains held out from model fitting but is not an untouched confirmatory test. This is not an independent learner-essay accuracy or learning-effectiveness study. Model weights are not changed by this evaluation.

classifierConfidence.policy: A numeric synthetic-task probability is shown only for the ASCII tokenization-stable cohort with learned subject morphology used for calibration. Natural essay confidence remains unestablished.

selection.method: Seeded SHA-256 ordering of eligible official-test sentence IDs; first 300, before inspecting model predictions
selection.deduplication: Exact token sequences and document groups excluded against official train and dev, matching training/train_release.py policy. Sentences with UD tokens that cannot exactly align to original text are excluded before sampling.

fixture.scope: Held-out from model training, but drawn from the same public corpus used for model development/test reporting. This is neither a newly independent dataset nor an error-annotated learner-essay benchmark. Author/prompt independence is unverified.

naturalSyntax.sourceGenreMethod: Genre follows the official English Web Treebank sentence-ID prefix (answers, email, newsgroup, reviews, or weblog), documented by the pinned corpus README. Per-genre scores use every gold token in that family; tokenization mismatches and fallback tokens count as incorrect.
naturalSyntax.method: Exact original UTF-16 span alignment; unmatched or lexical-fallback tokens count as incorrect in all-gold metrics. Aligned-neural metrics condition on span matches and must be read with coverage. Basic UD exact relation labels; root self-loop decoded as gold head 0. No gold POS, heads, or features are sent to the worker.

learnedOutputEvidence.note: Difference from deterministic fallback demonstrates that the learned syntax path changes predictions; it alone does not prove better accuracy. Gold comparisons above measure correctness.
